classification.difficultyReason: Eliminates time for a downward launch, substitutes the landing coordinates to determine speed, then uses velocity components to find the impact angle.

content.prompt: A stone is thrown from the top of a $60\text{ m}$ cliff at an angle of $27^\circ$ below the horizontal. It lands in the ocean $35\text{ m}$ from the base of the cliff.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Taking the origin at the point of projection, show that the path has Cartesian equation $$y=-x\tan27^\circ-\frac{5x^2}{V^2\cos^227^\circ},$$ where $V$ is the initial speed.

answer.worked:
With the launch point as the origin and upward positive, 

$$\begin{aligned}\dot{x}&=V\cos27^\circ,\\\dot{y}&=-10t-V\sin27^\circ,\\x&=Vt\cos27^\circ,\\y&=-5t^2-Vt\sin27^\circ.\end{aligned}$$

 Hence $t=\dfrac{x}{V\cos27^\circ}$, so 

$$\begin{aligned}y&=-5\left(\frac{x}{V\cos27^\circ}\right)^2-V\left(\frac{x}{V\cos27^\circ}\right)\sin27^\circ\\y&=-\frac{x\sin27^\circ}{\cos27^\circ}-\frac{5x^2}{V^2\cos^227^\circ}\\y&=-x\tan27^\circ-\frac{5x^2}{V^2\cos^227^\circ}.\end{aligned}$$

At the landing point, $x=35$ and $y=-60$. 

$$\begin{aligned}-60&=-35\tan27^\circ-\frac{6125}{V^2\cos^227^\circ}\\\frac{6125}{V^2\cos^227^\circ}&=60-35\tan27^\circ\\V^2&=\frac{6125}{(60-35\tan27^\circ)\cos^227^\circ}\\V&=\sqrt{\frac{6125}{(60-35\tan27^\circ)\cos^227^\circ}}\\V&\approx13.5\text{ m/s}\quad\text{(1 d.p.).}\end{aligned}$$

children.label: ii
children.prompt: the direction of motion when it lands, to the nearest degree.

answer.worked:
Using the unrounded value of $V$ from part b(i), 

$$\begin{aligned}t&=\frac{35}{V\cos27^\circ}\approx2.90\text{ s},\\\dot{x}&=V\cos27^\circ\approx12.05\text{ m/s},\\\dot{y}&=-10t-V\sin27^\circ\approx-35.17\text{ m/s}.\end{aligned}$$

 If $\phi$ is the angle below the horizontal, 

$$\begin{aligned}\phi&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{|\dot{y}|}{\dot{x}}\right)\\\phi&\approx71^\circ\quad\text{(nearest degree).}\end{aligned}$$

 The direction is $71^\circ$ below the horizontal.
